newsitem.title: UK: Philip Morris up in London on lawsuit news.
newsitem.headline: Philip Morris up in London on lawsuit news.

text.p: Shares in Philip Morris led tobaccos higher following a U.S. court decision to throw out the bulk of a lawsuit in the state of Florida, dealers said.

Philip Morris was trading at $94-1/4 compared with its New York close of $92 after a judge late on Monday dismissed all the pre-1994 claims in the Medicaid suit brought against the tobacco industry by the state of Florida.

The court threw out the same damage claims that have been asserted by other states that have filed similar Medicaid reimbursement lawsuits, including restitution, fraud, and conspiracy,, Philip Morris said in a statement.
"Philip Morris is strong but I can see it going even higher in New York later today," one market maker said. "I can't see any reason for it not to be at least $3 better at the(U.S.)close," he added.
The U.S. court decision lifted other tobaccos, with RJR Nabisco Holdings up $1/2 at $27 while American Brand added $1/2 to $43-3/8.
